ruling.recommended_action: Send the case to a human reviewer to decide whether the 18:50–19:00 off-route segment was the agreed route; if it is found not covered, refund S$5.77 (4.09 km × $1.4100/km) as a voucher.
ruling.reasoning:
This is a metered RydeTAXI trip, so extra kilometres enter the fare [F7]. The trace settles that one off-route segment exists (RD-1): 18:50–19:00, 6.93 km driven where the optimal route covers 2.84 km, adding 4.09 km [F3]. It also settles that no qualifying traffic incident excuses the replaced stretch: RD-4(a) fails, and a speed band alone cannot exempt (G3), so KALLANG PAYA LEBAR EXPRESSWAY band 2 during 18:24–18:50 corroborates nothing more [F12][F15].

RD-5 is the element I must read, and the record does not let me settle it. The driver asked at 18:46 whether he could "go round via Defu Avenue 1" and the rider answered at 18:47 "Can lah, go ahead." [F8][F9][F10] — a rider message sent before the segment began at 18:50, so this is real consent to a specifically named road. Under the second kind of RD-5 scope, that agreement covers driving on Defu Avenue 1 only, and the record must tie this segment to that road. Nothing ties them: the fact table carries no road names for the driven path, no message places the car on Defu Avenue 1, and no stop is measured on it [F3][F8][F9]. Timing alone does not tie them (G13). The driver's post-trip statement naming the same road is not part of the chat and is not rider consent (G11) [F11]. With the segment neither tied to the agreed road nor placed elsewhere on the record, the finding is undetermined (G13), and because that finding changes the amount, the case goes to a person (RD-5, G12).

RD-3 gives no exemption either: the rider named no place and no stop was measured in the segment, so RD-3(a) does not apply to the way there [F3][F8][F9].

For the reviewer's information, the amount if the segment is held not covered: the trip rate is the distance fare ÷ distance km, $34.39 ÷ 24.39 km = $1.4100/km [F4][F7]; 4.09 km × $1.4100/km = $5.7669, i.e. $5.77 under RD-2. The billed excess-distance figure of $6.40 (4.54 km) is larger than the measured segment and is not the refund base; the remaining 0.45 km is unmatched corridor wobble outside any segment [F3][F4]. Waiting $0.11 is a metered waiting unit, not refunded [F5]; no surge [F6] and no unpublished item in the fare breakdown [F7].

RD-6 does not attach: the driver has 1 upheld dispute in 90 days but it is a no-show, not a route dispute (route_disputes_upheld_90d = 0), so no account flag is warranted on this record [F18]. Evidence status is insufficient only in the one sense that matters: the record carries no road name for the driven path, so it cannot tie the segment to Defu Avenue 1 (G13). SAFE: I read the complaint, both messages and the driver's statement; "Can lah" is agreement and the fare question is a billing complaint — nothing threatens, intimidates, harasses or alleges dangerous driving [F8][F9][F11], so safety_concern is none.
ruling.escalation_reason: segment finding undetermined for F3; evidence insufficient: No road-name or positioning record ties the 18:50–19:00 off-route segment to Defu Avenue 1, the only road the rider agreed to; the fact table carries no road names for the driven path, so the RD-5 scope of consent cannot be settled (G13).

segment_findings.reason: The driver asked at 18:46 for a route round via Defu Avenue 1 and the rider agreed at 18:47, before the segment began at 18:50 [F8][F9][F10]. That is a SPECIFIC named-road agreement, so under RD-5 it covers driving on Defu Avenue 1 only, and the record must tie this segment to that road. Nothing does: the fact table carries no road names for the driven path and no message places the car on Defu Avenue 1 [F3]. The driver's post-trip statement naming the same road is not rider consent and does not supply the link [F11][G11]. Neither tied to the agreed road nor placed elsewhere on the record, the segment is undetermined (G13); it changes the amount, so the case goes to a person.

rejected_claims.reason: The driver-side claim of no deviation and no charge fails on the record: the trace settles an off-route segment of +4.09 km on this metered RydeTAXI trip [F3][RD-1], and no traffic incident excuses the replaced stretch [F15][RD-4(a)]. His post-trip statement that the rider agreed verbally is not consent and cannot tie the segment to the agreed road [F11][RD-5][G11], so the segment is not simply excused — it remains undetermined.

The rider-side claim that the whole extra fare should be struck is not established: the rider did agree before the segment to the driver's proposed route round via Defu Avenue 1 [F8][F9][F10], so this is not a case of no consent at all, and the billed excess-distance figure of $6.40 covers 4.54 km, of which only 4.09 km is attributable to the one measured off-route segment [F3][F4][RD-2]. At most the segment's extra_km at the trip rate are in issue, which is why the amount is escalated rather than granted in full.
